While our 90% confidence intervals capture a significant range of probable outcomes, certain unforeseen events or "black swan" scenarios could push the actual results beyond these boundaries. On the upside, an unexpected breakthrough in technology, a sudden surge in economic growth, significant de-escalation of global tensions, or unpredicted positive policy changes could drive the value well above the upper bounds of our forecasts. Conversely, outcomes could fall significantly below our lower bounds due to events such as a severe economic recession, a major geopolitical crisis, a widespread natural disaster, or unforeseen regulatory crackdowns. These extreme events, by their very nature, are difficult to quantify within standard probabilistic models, representing external risks to our stated intervals.
